summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, COPD, chronic kidney disease, and insulin-dependent diabetes was admitted for acute-on-chronic systolic heart failure exacerbated by dietary indiscretion. He presented with shortness of breath, orthopnea, bilateral leg edema, and chest tightness. Chest imaging showed moderate pulmonary edema, and labs revealed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine. He was treated with intravenous diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and optimized on heart failure medications including digoxin and losartan. His kidney function improved, and his volume status stabilized. Diabetes management was adjusted with increased insulin dosing, and pravastatin and benzonatate were added. He was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions on daily weights, low-salt diet, and close follow-up.
